text: Continuous Integration is a common practice in modern software development. Developers regularly add their code to a shared repository, and every change triggers automated builds. This means the software is compiled and tested without anyone doing it manually. During these builds, the system runs tests to check that everything works correctly. Because problems are found quickly, teams can catch issues early, before they become bigger and harder to fix. CI pipelines organise all these steps, from building to testing to reporting results. As a result, developers receive fast feedback and can keep improving the software with confidence.
